title.narrative: Provide lifesaving WASH services to most vulnerable drought-affected populations in Jowhar rural areas of middle Shabelle region.

description.narrative:
ltp style="" class=""gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtAccording to the WASH Cluster, more than 8 million people are affected by poor and deteriorating WASH conditions and require severe and extreme humanitarian WASH assistance, which has been exacerbated by Somalia's recurring drought and conflict. WASH is one of the two main drivers of humanitarian needs in Somalia, highlighting WASH's growing importance in determining the severity of humanitarian needs for both IDPs and non-IDPs. As a result, SHEDU proposes a project to provide life-saving and fundamental WASH services. Through the rehabilitation and/or extension of existing water infrastructures, and the establishment of gender-balanced water management committees to ensure service continuity, appropriate operation, and maintenance, as well as the strengthening of women's leadership and participation in WASH projects through capacity building. SHEDU created an intervention to support the 2023 Somalia Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and efforts to address the needs of the most vulnerable displaced communities affected, by drought, with a focus on the Jowhar in the Middle Shabelle region.ltbrgt As a result, during dry seasons, Jowhar rural villages populations rely on water trucking for survival or truck for almost 3km to a nearby boreholes specially those who are far away from river Shabelle. This solution is prohibitively expensive and, in terms of long-term growth, unsustainable. The proposed project aims to address both the immediate needs of drought-affected households by improving access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene through rehabilitation of strategic water facilities both benefiting both community and health/Nutrition centres, household level hygiene promotion, and the establishment and reinforcement of WASH management structures to ensure sustainable WASH services for target populations.ltbrgt SHEDU's proposed WASH activities will focus on both short-term and long-term interventions, such as addressing the need for better hygiene practices through promotion campaigns focusing on soap-free handwashing and menstrual hygiene education for women and addressing the need for better hygiene practices through promotion campaigns focusing on soap-free handwashing. In addition, 50 flood proof latrines with handwashing facilities and lockable doors on the inside and outside to ensure user privacy will be constructed. The newly constructed latrines will benefit 400 individuals hence targeting per latrine to be used by 8 persons. Organizing hygiene promotion and training campaigns, as well as providing necessary hygiene items such as female menstrual kits the establishment gender-balanced water management committees in the rehabilitated /newly Constructed water assets in Jowhar rural villages is intended to ensure service continuity, proper operation, and maintenance.ltbrgt SHEDU will also provide emergency clean water access through water trucking in four rural communities in Jowhar west and east thus Xayoley, Maxaa ka rebay,Garaash,Towfiq village and Xaansholey whereby a total population of 5100 ltspan lang="EN-US"gtindividualslt/spangt 0r 850HHs will benefit that trek for long to get water and had less humanitarian assistance.ltbrgt Distribution of solid waste collection tools (Wheelbarrow (x1), Pickaxe (x1), Shovel/spade (x2), Brooms (x4), and Rakes (x3) for clean-up campaigns to rural communities and health centres for solid waste management (with special consideration given to persons with disabilities in selecting those who will work on their behalf).lt/spangt
